questions_and_answers.question_text: What NEW meaning of huì is introduced here?
Which adverbs can clarify the degree of certainty with huì?
In what kind of sentences is this -de generally used?
What are the two meanings of yìfāngmiàn...yìfāngmiàn...?
Write the Chinese for "That's not very likely."
Why needn't you use the sentence-final -de a lot?

answers.answer_text: Because most native Běijīng speakers feel it is southern Chinese or a carry-over from southern dialects — it is enough to understand it.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "If you tell him he'll get angry."

answers.answer_text: Nǐ gàosu ta, tā huì shēngqìde.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "He watches television while eating."

answers.answer_text: Tā yìfāngmiàn kàn diànshì, yìfāngmiàn chī dōngxi.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Does it look to you as if it might rain today?"

answers.answer_text: Nǐ kàn jīntian huì bu huì xià yǔ?

articles.text:
10. A: Nǐ zài Zhōngguo zhù           If you live in China for two years
       liǎngnián, yídìng huì          you're sure to learn Chinese
       xuéhǎo Zhōngwénde.             very well.
    B: Shì a, yìfāngmiàn kěyi        Yes, on the one hand I can learn
       xuéhǎo Zhōngwén, yìfāngmiàn    Chinese well, and on the other hand
       yě kěyi duō zhīdao yìdiǎnr     I can find out more things about
       Zhōngguóde shìqing.            China.

Notes on No. 10

huì: "might, be likely to, will." You already know huì meaning "to know how to, can." Here you see huì used in a NEW way, to express LIKELIHOOD. Huì ranges in meaning from possible to probable to definite. Various adverbs can be added before huì to clarify the degree of certainty: yídìng, "definitely"; dàgài, "probably"; yěxǔ, "perhaps."

huì
Yǐjing shíèrdiǎn bàn le, zhè     It's half past twelve. Who would come
shíhou shéi huì lái ne?          at this hour?
Nǐde chènshān zāngle bú yàojǐn,  It doesn't matter that your shirt got
wǒ huì gěi nǐ xǐ.                dirty. I'll wash it for you.

bú huì
Bú dà huì ba?                    That's not very likely.
Dàgài bú huì shi ta.             It's probably not him.

huì...ma?
Tā huì qù ma? Tā huì qù.         Will he go? He'll go.

huì bu huì
Míngtian tā huì bu huì lái?      Will he come tomorrow?
Nǐ kàn jīntian huì bu huì xià    Does it look to you as if it might
yǔ?                              rain today?

nǐ huì xuéhǎode: So far you have seen -de used as a marker of possession or of modification, and in the shi...de construction. Here it is used in an ENTIRELY NEW way: at the END of a sentence, -de can mean "THAT'S THE WAY THE SITUATION IS." Generally, this -de is used in emphatic assertions or denials, especially those expressing probability, necessity, desire, etc.

Usage note: Unless the sentence contains shi, the majority of native Běijīng speakers seem to feel that this -de is nánfāng huà, southern Chinese, or a carry-over from southern dialects. You needn't try to use it a lot; it will be enough for you to UNDERSTAND this -de.

(1) Sentences with shi in the sense of "it is that..."
Wǒ shi bú qùde.                  I'm not going.
Zhèige, nǐ shi zhīdaode.         This you know.

(2) Sentences with an auxiliary verb (huì, néng, yào, yīnggāi, etc.)
Nǐ gàosu ta, tā huì shēngqìde.   If you tell him he'll get angry.
Wǒmen zǒng yǒu yìtiān yào huí    There will come a day when we will go
dàlùde.                          back to the mainland.

(3) Others: sentences with adverbs like yídìng, with potential resultative verbs, with -guo, etc.
Zhèixiē shū yídìng xūyàode.      These books are definitely needed.
Bú yàojǐnde.                     It doesn't matter.

yìfāngmiàn...yìfāngmiàn...: This has two meanings: (1) "on the one hand..., on the other hand..." and (2) "doing...while doing...."

Tā yìfāngmiàn kàn diànshì,       He watches television while eating.
yìfāngmiàn chī dōngxi.
